title: Go
events_chronological: Supermarket checkout girl Ronna takes Simon's Christmas Eve shift because he is driving to Las Vegas and she is about to be evicted.
Narcotics detective Burke catches soap actors Adam and Zack buying and puts them in wires to make a case against their dealer.
Adam and Zack come to Simon's till asking for twenty hits of ecstasy.
Ronna takes the deal herself and goes with her friend Claire to Simon's dealer, Todd Gaines.
Todd refuses to front the drugs, so Ronna leaves Claire in his flat as collateral and takes the pills on credit.
In the car park Ronna spots Burke waiting with Adam and Zack and realises the buy is a sting.
Ronna flushes the ecstasy and sells the pair crushed cold remedies instead.
Simon and his friend Marcus talk their way into a free Las Vegas suite, a wedding chapel and a strip club.
Simon sleeps with two women and leaves a hotel room on fire.
Burke takes Adam and Zack home to dinner, where his real interest turns out to be signing them into a pyramid scheme with his wife Irene.
Ronna goes to a warehouse rave to unload the rest of the aspirin on strangers.
Simon takes a security guard's gun in the club, shoots the bouncer through the arm, and the four run for the car.
The club's owner chases them out into the desert and shoots the borrowed Ferrari to pieces.
Todd works out that he has been cheated and comes after Ronna at the rave, and she runs out into the road.
Adam and Zack, driving home, are the ones who hit her, and they panic and leave her in an alley.
Simon gets back to Los Angeles and Todd corners him over the money, and Simon shoots Todd through the arm.
Ronna comes round in the alley and reaches the diner on Christmas morning, where all three stories meet.
syuzhet_notes: The film tells the same Christmas Eve three times over, once per group, rewinding to the supermarket at the start of each chapter. Told-order bullets 1-8 are Ronna's night, bullets 9-12 restart the evening in Las Vegas with Simon, and bullets 13-15 restart it again with Adam and Zack, revealing that the car that hit Ronna at bullet 8 was theirs. Only the last two bullets belong to a stretch all three strands share.
fabula_notes: The three chapters are largely simultaneous, so a single chronology has to interleave scenes the film keeps in separate blocks; the ordering here follows the few shared markers - the buy, the rave, the collision, Christmas morning. That Burke had already turned Adam and Zack before they walked into the supermarket is only established in the third chapter.
